ruling.recommended_action: Route to human review: verify the 09:00–09:11 off-route segment against the chat record and the driver's conduct; if the human finds no safety ground, execute a partial refund of the 5.14 km unexempted segment (5.14 km × $1.4102/km = $7.25) and record the driver's discourtesy; issue any refund as a Ryde voucher.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip was a metered RydeTAXI job: the fare record shows $44.17 total with a $30.22 distance component over 21.43 km, so any route deviation flows into the fare rather than being absorbed by a fixed quote [F7][RD-2]. One off-route segment exists, 09:00–09:11, 6.89 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.75 km, +5.14 km and up to 1481 m off route [F3][RD-1]. No exemption applies: there is no incident on the replaced stretch [F14], and the only speed-band records are PIE band 5 (40–49 km/h) and KPE band 4 (30–39 km/h), not the band 1–2 severe-congestion reading [F12][F13][RD-4]. The chat is complete and fully timestamped [F10], and it contains no rider message before 09:00:10 agreeing to anything — the rider's only message, at 09:04, is a challenge ("Why are we going this way? This is not the route on the app.") [F8], and the driver's post-trip claim that the GPS rerouted him is a statement, not consent [F11][RD-5]. So on the route elements alone the segment counts and the arithmetic would be 5.14 km × $1.4102/km = $7.25 [F3][F4][RD-2]; the remaining 0.41 km of billed excess (5.55 km, $7.83) is corridor/matching mileage that RD-2 expressly does not refund [F4][RD-2], and the $0.11 waiting unit is meter-accrued waiting on a RydeTAXI stop under RD-3(c) and is not refunded [F5][F7][RD-3].

However, the safety screen does not come out clean. At 09:05, one minute after the rider's route question [F8], the driver wrote "Shut up and let me drive." [F9]. Read in context, that is a hostile remark aimed at the rider, silencing her after she raised a concern — abusive language under the code of conduct, which bars "abuse of any kind", and enough to mark this case as suspected harassment rather than mere rudeness in a route argument [F9][SAFE-1]. A refund for unexempted mileage can only execute after a human has seen that [F9][SAFE-1].

The evidence is otherwise sufficient to settle the route elements (measured segment, complete timestamped chat, fare records) [F3][F10][F4], and the RD-4 incident screen is settled by the trace [F14]; the RD-3 and RD-5 questions are settled by the absence of any pre-segment rider message [F8][RD-5]. But because the safety concern is suspected, the policy takes the case out of automated adjudication and into human hands [F9][SAFE-1], so no amount is fixed here. No account flag is warranted in any event: the driver's profile shows 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days, so the RD-6 "repeated" predicate is absent [F17][RD-6].

segment_findings.reason: The only rider message in the complete, fully timestamped chat is the 09:04 route challenge [F8][F10], sent four minutes after the segment began at 09:00 [F3]; nothing in the rider's words grants consent before the segment, and the driver's post-trip 'GPS rerouted me' claim is a statement, not rider consent [F11]. Under RD-5 a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment counts, so the segment's extra_km are refundable under RD-2. No stop was requested or measured, so RD-3(a) cannot exempt it, and RD-4 fails for want of a qualifying incident or band 1–2 reading [F14][F12][F13].

rejected_claims.reason: Rejected as to amount: the billed excess of $7.83 covers 5.55 km [F4], but RD-2 refunds only the unexempted segment's extra_km, so the segment figure is 5.14 km × $1.4102/km = $7.25 and the 0.41 km corridor/matching difference is not refundable [F3][F4][RD-2]. No amount is executed here in any case because the case escalates on SAFE-1 [F9].

Accepted in substance, but it changes the outcome: the rider's reading of F9 is right that the words are abusive and require a human [F9][F8][SAFE-1], which is exactly why the ruling is escalate rather than the automated refund_partial the rider asked for.
Not pressed and not applied: 0 upheld route disputes in 90 d means RD-6's 'repeated' predicate is absent, so no flag_account issues on route grounds [F17][RD-6].

Rejected as a route defence but its premise is correct: bands 5 and 4 on the PIE and KPE are above band 1–2 and band evidence alone does not exempt, so the segment falls back to RD-2 [F12][F13][RD-4]; the band facts do not excuse the deviation [F3][RD-1].
Rejected as a defence and fatal to the driver: no pre-segment rider message exists in the complete chat [F8][F10], so RD-5 yields no exemption and the segment counts [F3][RD-5].
Accepted only in part: 0 upheld route disputes in 90 d means no RD-6 flag [F17][RD-6], but the driver's F9 remark remains a conduct matter for the human reviewer under SAFE-1 [F9].

Rejected: F9 is a rider-directed hostile remark made one minute after the rider raised a route concern [F9][F8]; read in context it is abuse under the code of conduct and is at least 'suspected' harassment, so SAFE-1 removes the case from automated adjudication [RD-1 not applicable to safety; SAFE-1].
